parts.title: The Last Stretch
parts.text: After eleven years aboard the starship Meridian, Zora finally saw the planet her people hoped to **colonize**. Scientists had searched for centuries before finding a world that was **habitable**: not too hot, not too cold, and rich with liquid water. The ship had crossed an **interstellar** gulf so wide that even light needed four years to cross it. Now its **propulsion** engines fired in long bursts, slowing the great vessel for landing.

parts.title: Life Aboard
parts.text: Zora's best friend Matteo worked in the garden **module**, a round chamber glowing with purple lamps. His crops grew in water instead of soil, a **hydroponic** system that fed three hundred people. Nkechi, the ship's mechanic, explained that the spinning ring created artificial **gravity**, which kept everyone's feet on the floor. Still, years of **confinement** inside metal walls had made the passengers restless and short-tempered.

parts.title: A Test of Courage
parts.text: Two days before landing, a **shortage** of spare filters threatened the water system. "We must **innovate**," Nkechi told the friends, "because nobody can send help." Together they built a replacement from scrap mesh and a cooking pot. Then Matteo, wearing a bulky suit, had to step through the **airlock** to reach the outer pipe, his heart pounding as the door sealed behind him. When clear water finally flowed, every hopeful **settler** aboard cheered.

parts.title: Touchdown
parts.text: The Meridian settled onto the new world with a gentle shudder. Zora pressed her hand against the window and watched red dust drift past. She thought about the people who had built the ship, none of whom would ever see this sky. The journey had taught her that a home is something people make together, one careful decision at a time.

definitions.meaning1: To settle in a new place and make it a home for your people. Example: Explorers hoped to colonize the island and build farms along its coast.
definitions.meaning2: (Of plants or animals) to spread into and live in a new area. Example: Tiny mosses began to colonize the bare rocks after the flood.

definitions.meaning1: To create new ideas or new ways of doing something. Example: Engineers must innovate when the old tools no longer solve a problem.
definitions.studentChallenge: The company hired young designers who could ___ and invent better bicycles.

definitions.meaning1: Safe and suitable to live in. Example: After the repairs, the damaged cabin was habitable again.
definitions.studentChallenge: Scientists search for planets that are ___ for humans.

definitions.meaning1: Happening or traveling between the stars. Example: An interstellar voyage would take longer than a human lifetime.
definitions.studentChallenge: Writers love to imagine ___ travel between distant star systems.

definitions.meaning1: The force or system that pushes a vehicle forward. Example: The rocket's propulsion system burned fuel to lift it off the pad.
definitions.studentChallenge: The submarine's ___ comes from a large spinning propeller.

definitions.meaning1: A separate, self-contained unit that forms part of a larger structure. Example: The astronauts slept in a small module attached to the main station.
definitions.meaning2: A unit of study within a course. Example: Our science class ends with a module on volcanoes.
definitions.studentChallenge: The crew connected the sleeping ___ to the rest of the station.

definitions.meaning1: Growing plants in water filled with nutrients instead of in soil. Example: The school's hydroponic garden grew lettuce on shelves in the science lab.
definitions.studentChallenge: Without any soil, the ___ farm grew tomatoes in trays of nutrient-rich water.

definitions.meaning1: The force that pulls objects toward each other, such as pulling things toward the ground. Example: Gravity keeps the moon circling Earth.
definitions.meaning2: Seriousness or great importance. Example: The judge spoke about the gravity of the crime.
definitions.studentChallenge: On the moon, ___ is weaker, so astronauts can leap high.

definitions.meaning1: The state of being kept inside a small or enclosed space. Example: After days of confinement in the tent, the campers were desperate to go outside.
definitions.studentChallenge: Long ___ in the tiny cabin made the sailors restless.

definitions.meaning1: A small sealed room with two doors that lets people pass between places with different air pressure. Example: Astronauts wait in the airlock before they step out into space.
definitions.studentChallenge: The astronaut sealed the inner door of the ___ before opening the outer one.

definitions.meaning1: A person who moves to a new place to make a home there. Example: Early settlers built their houses from the trees they cleared.
definitions.studentChallenge: The first ___ planted crops and built cabins beside the river.

definitions.meaning1: A situation in which there is not enough of something. Example: A shortage of rain left the farmers' fields dry and cracked.
definitions.studentChallenge: A ___ of bread at the store left the shelves empty by noon.
